facts: The complainant parked his motorcycle outside his house at night. In the morning it was gone. CCTV shows the accused pushing it away down the lane and riding off. The accused had no permission to take it and did not return it.

defenses.argument: The prosecution has failed to prove the essential ingredient of 'dishonest intention' (animus furandi). Mere unauthorized movement of property, without evidence of a specific intent to permanently deprive the owner or appropriate it as one's own, does not constitute theft under Section 303. The accused may have moved the motorcycle for reasons other than dishonesty, such as moving it to clear an obstruction or due to a misunderstanding of ownership rights.
